instruction:
Repository: /luxon (luxon JS date library v1.20.0). Work ONLY inside /luxon. bash available (node, npx jest, npx babel-node; node_modules installed).

GOAL: Fix an injected bug in /luxon/src/duration.js so that the hidden test `Duration#normalize can convert all unit pairs` passes. The repository already has related tests; look at /luxon/test/duration/math.test.js (search for `normalize`) to see the existing expectations, and read the `normalize()`, `shiftTo()`, `normalizeValues()`, `convert()` and the conversion matrices (lowOrderMatrix / casualMatrix / accurateMatrix) in /luxon/src/duration.js. One of those matrices or the conversion helper has been subtly changed (e.g. a wrong factor, a missing/extra unit entry, a wrong index) so that normalizing some unit pair gives a wrong result.

METHOD:
1. Read /luxon/src/duration.js lines 1-160 (the matrices and convert/normalizeValues) carefully, and the normalize/shiftTo methods (~lines 540-630).
2. Write a temp babel-node probe script INSIDE /luxon (e.g. /luxon/tmp_dur.js; babel-node only compiles files under cwd; delete it afterwards) that, for every ordered pair of units [years, quarters, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds], builds `Duration.fromObject({ [from]: 1 })` (and also a few multi-unit cases) and checks:
   - `d.normalize().toObject()` contains no negative leftover and the value equals the mathematically expected conversion using the casual matrix (years=365 days, quarters=91 days, months=30 days, weeks=7 days, days=24h, ...) — i.e. 1 year = 12 months = 52 weeks = 365 days = 8760 hours = 525600 minutes = 31536000 seconds = 31536000000 ms; 1 quarter = 3 months = 13 weeks = 91 days; 1 month = 4 weeks = 30 days; 1 week = 7 days; 1 day = 24 h; 1 h = 60 min; 1 min = 60 s; 1 s = 1000 ms.
   - `Duration.fromObject({ [from]: 1 }).shiftTo(to).toObject()` matches the same expectation, and `Duration.fromObject({ [from]: 1, [to]: 1 }).normalize()` keeps both units with the right values.
   - also check the accurate matrix (`{ conversionAccuracy: "longterm" }`) conversions for a couple of pairs.
   Print a table of any pair whose result is wrong, with expected vs actual.
3. Fix the single wrong constant/entry in /luxon/src/duration.js with the MINIMAL change (do not reformat, do not restructure).
4. Re-run the probe until all pairs are correct, then run `cd /luxon && npx jest test/duration 2>&1 | tail -30` and the full `npx jest 2>&1 | tail -25`. Known pre-existing failures that MUST remain the only failures: 2 tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (`DateTime#toFormat('FFF') returns a medium date/time representation without seconds` and `DateTime#toFormat('FFFF') ...`).
5. Run `npx prettier --list-different src/duration.js` (must print nothing) and `git diff` in /luxon; report it.

CONSTRAINTS: Do NOT modify anything under /luxon/test. Do NOT modify /luxon/src/impl/util.js, /luxon/src/datetime.js or /luxon/src/interval.js (other agents are editing those concurrently). No git commit/checkout/stash/restore.

REPORT: the exact buggy line before/after, the probe table evidence, the diff, jest results before/after, and confirmation that no previously-passing test now fails.

Repository: /luxon (luxon JS date library v1.20.0). Work ONLY inside /luxon. You have bash (node, npx jest, npx babel-node available; node_modules installed).

GOAL: Find and fix an injected bug in /luxon/src/impl/util.js. Evidence: the hidden test `DateTime#plus works across the 100 barrier when passing through February` must pass after the fix. The repository already contains a passing test `DateTime#plus works across the 100 barrier` in /luxon/test/datetime/math.test.js (line ~92) which does `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 2 })` and expects year 100, month 1, day 2. The hidden test is a variant involving February, e.g. something like `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ months: 2 })` or `.plus({ days: 60 })` expecting the correct February date in year 100 (note: year 100 is NOT a leap year, 100 % 100 == 0 and 100 % 400 != 0).

METHOD (be systematic, do not guess):
1. Read /luxon/src/impl/util.js fully and /luxon/src/datetime.js function `adjustTime` (around line 124) plus `objToTS`/`objToLocalTS` usage. util.js is a small file; one of its functions has been subtly changed relative to correct behaviour. Candidates: objToLocalTS (legacy 0-99 year handling), daysInMonth, daysInYear, isLeapYear, floorMod, parseInteger, untruncateYear, weeksInWeekYear, roundTo, padStart, signedOffset, formatOffset, asNumber, normalizeObject, bestBy, parseMillis.
2. Empirically test with babel-node (create a temp script INSIDE /luxon, e.g. /luxon/tmp_probe.js, because babel-node only compiles files under cwd; delete it when done). Examples to check against hand-computed expectations:
   - `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ months: 2 })` should be 0100-02-28T00:00:00 (year 100, month 2, day 28)
   - `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ months: 1 })` should be 0100-01-31
   - `DateTime.fromISO("0099-11-30").plus({ months: 3 })` should be 0100-02-28
   - `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ days: 60 })` should be 0100-03-01 (Jan 31 days + Feb 28 days = 59, so +60 = Mar 1)
   - `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 2 })` must stay 0100-01-02 (existing test)
   - `DateTime.fromISO("0100-01-02").minus({ day: 2 })` must stay 0099-12-31 (existing test at math.test.js line ~169)
   - `DateTime.fromISO("2016-03-31").plus({ months: 1 })` -> 2016-04-30, `DateTime.fromISO("2016-01-31").plus({months:1})` -> 2016-02-29, `DateTime.fromISO("2017-01-31").plus({months:1})` -> 2017-02-28, `DateTime.fromObject({year:2016,month:2,day:29}).plus({years:1})` -> 2017-02-28
   - also test the `daysInMonth`/`isLeapYear` behaviour for years like 0, 4, 100, 200, 400, 1900, 2000 via `DateTime.fromObject({year: X, month: 2}).daysInMonth`
   - also check `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31T00:00:00").toISO()` round trips and `DateTime.fromObject({year: 99, month: 12, day: 31}).toISO()`
3. Identify which function in util.js produces a wrong value, and fix it with the MINIMAL change that restores correct behaviour (do not reformat, do not touch other files, do not touch anything under /luxon/test).
4. Verify: `cd /luxon && npx jest test/datetime 2>&1 | tail -30` and then the full `npx jest 2>&1 | tail -20`. Baseline known failures (must remain the ONLY failures): 2 tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js named `DateTime#toFormat('FFF') returns a medium date/time representation without seconds` and `DateTime#toFormat('FFFF') returns a long date/time representation without seconds` (ICU-related). Also run `npx prettier --list-different src/impl/util.js` and make sure it prints nothing.
5. Also run `git diff` in /luxon and report it.

REPORT: the exact buggy line(s) before and after, the evidence (probe outputs) that pinned the bug, the final `git diff`, the jest results before/after, and confirmation that no previously-passing test now fails.

Repository: /luxon. Work ONLY inside /luxon. bash available (node, npx jest, npx babel-node).

URGENT, TIME-CRITICAL. GOAL: fix the injected bug in /luxon/src/duration.js so that `Duration#normalize can convert all unit pairs` passes.

DIAGNOSIS: in the `casualMatrix` object literal at the top of /luxon/src/duration.js (~lines 30-59), the `quarters` entry is missing its `seconds` conversion:

```js
      quarters: {
        months: 3,
        weeks: 13,
        days: 91,
        hours: 91 * 24,
        minutes: 91 * 24 * 60,
        milliseconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
      },
```

It must be:

```js
      quarters: {
        months: 3,
        weeks: 13,
        days: 91,
        hours: 91 * 24,
        minutes: 91 * 24 * 60,
        seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60,
        milliseconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
      },
```

(`convert()` looks up `matrix[toUnit][fromUnit]`, so converting seconds into quarters / normalizing `{ seconds, quarters }` currently yields NaN.)

STEPS:
1. Read /luxon/src/duration.js lines 1-110 and confirm the missing entry (also check `accurateMatrix.quarters` — it should already have `seconds`; do not change it if it does).
2. Apply the minimal edit with edit_file, adding exactly the line `        seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60,` between the `minutes` and `milliseconds` lines of `casualMatrix.quarters`. Do not reformat anything else.
3. CONCURRENCY: another agent (sub-5) may be editing this same file. After your edit, re-read the file and confirm the line is present; if it was overwritten, re-apply (up to 3 attempts, `sleep 5` between). At the end, re-read and report the final content of the `casualMatrix.quarters` block.
4. VERIFY with a temp babel-node script created INSIDE /luxon (e.g. /luxon/tmp_q.js; babel-node only compiles files under cwd; delete it afterwards). For every ordered pair of units [years, quarters, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds] check that `Duration.fromObject({ [from]: 1, [to]: 1 }).normalize().toObject()` has no NaN and matches the casual-matrix expectation (1 year = 12 months = 52 weeks = 365 days = 8760 h = 525600 min = 31536000 s = 31536000000 ms; 1 quarter = 3 months = 13 weeks = 91 days = 2184 h = 131040 min = 7862400 s = 7862400000 ms; 1 month = 4 weeks = 30 days; 1 week = 7 days; 1 day = 24 h; 1 h = 60 min; 1 min = 60 s; 1 s = 1000 ms). Also check `Duration.fromObject({ seconds: 1, quarters: 1 }).normalize().toObject()` and `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).shiftTo("seconds").seconds === 7862400`. Print any failing pair.
5. Run `cd /luxon && npx jest test/duration 2>&1 | tail -20` and then `npx jest 2>&1 | tail -20`. Known pre-existing failures that MUST remain the only failures: the 2 tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (`DateTime#toFormat('FFF') returns a medium date/time representation without seconds`, `DateTime#toFormat('FFFF') ...`). Run `npx prettier --list-different src/duration.js` (must print nothing).

CONSTRAINTS: do NOT modify anything under /luxon/test; do NOT modify src/impl/util.js, src/datetime.js, src/interval.js or src/zones/*; no git commit/checkout/stash/restore.

REPORT (brief): the final `casualMatrix.quarters` block, probe results, jest summary, whether the edit had to be re-applied.
